title: Create real processes with fork, exec, and wait
brief: Decode wait statuses, fork children that report back through pipes, and run real programs with output captured from a pipe.
hints: `os.fork()` returns twice. It returns 0 in the child and the child's pid in the parent, so `if pid == 0:` is the child's branch.
End every child with `os._exit(code)` inside `try`/`finally`. A child that returns from your function would run the rest of the test harness a second time.
A pipe read ends with an empty `bytes` only after every copy of the write end is closed. Close the write end in the parent before you read.
In the child, `os.dup2(w, 1)` makes the pipe the child's stdout. `os.execvp` keeps file descriptors 0, 1, and 2 across the exec.
If `os.execvp` fails, it raises. Let `finally: os._exit(127)` run, and the parent sees exit code 127, the shell's "command not found".
`os.WIFEXITED(status)` and `os.WEXITSTATUS(status)` decode a normal exit. `os.WIFSIGNALED(status)` and `os.WTERMSIG(status)` decode a death by signal.
